nodes.content: Design a multi-region secret broker reconciling emergency credential revocation, partition availability, and rollback-safe rotation.
requirements: Revoked credentials become unusable within 60 seconds, including during network partitions and broker replica rollback.
Unrevoked workloads maintain 99.9% authentication success during 30-second regional partitions overlapping credential rotation.

nodes.content: Issue 50-second quorum-signed leases refreshed every 10 seconds; validate locally with trusted clocks, TPM-pinned epochs, and 60-second dual-key overlap.
Can partitioned brokers preserve rotation availability without renewing 50-second leases for credentials revoked elsewhere?
TPM clocks stay within two seconds of wall time despite replica rollback, enabling 30-second partition availability without renewing revoked leases.
Simulate remote revocations during 30-second partitioned rotations with two-second clock drift and replica rollback; measure cutoff and healthy-login success.
Run PartitionRotate-30 fault tests with 10,000 logins, remote revocations, two-second clock drift, and replica rollback; record cutoff and success.
PartitionRotate-30 achieved 98.7% healthy-login success: late partitions outlasted dual-key overlap before the isolated region received the next key.
Pre-stage next keys 90 seconds early; 10-second refresh of 50-second quorum leases should deliver ≥99.9% healthy logins without partition renewals.
Replay PartitionRotate-30 late-partition failures with 90-second key pre-staging, 50-second leases, and 10-second refresh; measure authentication success and revocation cutoff.
PartitionRotate-30 replay achieved 99.92% healthy-login success; revoked leases expired within 52 seconds under partition and replica rollback.
Adopt 90-second key pre-staging with 50-second quorum leases: replay meets both targets after the earlier late-partition overlap failures.
Run 100,000-login PartitionRotate-30 regression on adopted leases with remote revocations, two-second drift, and rollback; measure cutoff and success.
PartitionRotate-30 regression report contains 100,000-login cutoff and success metrics, plus partition, clock-drift, and rollback traces.
How can a rolled-back broker enforce the 60-second revocation cutoff while partitioned from the revocation quorum?
Deploy region-local HSM verification gateways independent of broker replicas, enforcing 50-second leases and pre-staged keys against monotonic revocation counters.
Implement regional HSM gateways, preload next keys 90 seconds early, pin revocation epochs, and block renewals without cross-region quorum.
Use PartitionRotate-30 regression traces as fixtures to test HSM gateway epoch pinning, 50-second lease expiry, and pre-staged keys.
HSM gateway conformance report records PartitionRotate-30 results for epoch pinning, lease expiry, key pre-staging, revocation cutoff, and login success.
Audit HSM gateway conformance metrics against both SLOs, reproducing partition and rollback traces to check the gateway design.
Conformance audit found HSM gateways rejected pre-staged rotation keys with future epochs during partitions, yielding 98.8% healthy-login success.
Can gateways accept pre-staged future-epoch keys during partitions without permitting rollback to bypass pinned revocation counters?
Separating signed rotation schedules from monotonic revocation counters should achieve ≥99.9% logins and ≤60-second revocation cutoff with 90-second pre-staging.
Replay PartitionRotate-30 with signed rotation schedules and monotonic HSM revocation counters; roll back partitioned brokers, measure login success and cutoff.
PartitionRotate-30 replay yielded 99.94% healthy-login success and a 52-second maximum revocation cutoff during partitioned broker rollback.
Revive HSM gateways with separate signed rotation schedules and monotonic revocation counters, resolving future-epoch rejection while meeting both targets.
Compare TPM-pinned brokers with revised HSM gateways using both reports and PartitionRotate-30 replay metrics for cutoff and success.
PartitionRotate-30 comparison: TPM-pinned brokers achieved 99.92% success; revised HSM gateways achieved 99.94%; both capped revocation at 52 seconds.
Combine quorum-signed 50-second leases with regional HSM gateways, decoupled signed rotation schedules, and hardware-pinned revocation counters.
How can partitioned regions accept pre-staged rotation keys while hardware-pinned counters reject revoked leases after broker rollback?
HSM gateways separating pre-staged keys from pinned revocation counters should achieve ≥99.9% logins and ≤52-second cutoff using quorum-signed 50-second leases.
Replay n11's PartitionRotate-30 traces through HSM gateways with pre-staged schedules and quorum leases; measure revocation cutoff and login success.
PartitionRotate-30 replay achieved 99.82% healthy-login success; HSM verification queues saturated at rotation boundaries, while revocation cutoff remained 52 seconds.
Four-way HSM sharding with preverified rotation signatures should clear boundary queues, reaching ≥99.9% logins without extending the 52-second cutoff.
Shard regional HSM verification four ways, preverify rotation schedules, then replay boundary partitions and rollbacks against both SLOs.
Replay PartitionRotate-30 with four HSM shards and preverified schedules; record healthy-login success, verification queue depth, and revocation cutoff.
PartitionRotate-30 with four HSM shards achieved 99.95% healthy-login success, 8-ms p99 queue wait, and 52-second maximum revocation cutoff.
Adopt four-shard HSM gateways, preverified schedules, and 50-second quorum leases: queue saturation resolved; 99.95% success, 52-second cutoff.
Implement four-shard HSM gateways with preverified rotation schedules, monotonic revocation counters, and 50-second quorum leases; run partition-and-rollback canaries.
SecretBroker v1.0 includes four-shard HSM gateways, preverified rotation schedules, pinned revocation counters, 50-second quorum leases, and partition-and-rollback canary traces.
Use software-verified, 45-second quorum-signed capabilities with TPM-clock expiry and 90-second pre-staged rotation keys, reserving HSMs for revocation attestation.
Prototype TPM-clock capability checks with HSM-attested revocation floors; replay partitioned rotations and rollback, measuring cutoff and login success.
Replay PartitionRotate-30 against software capabilities and SecretBroker v1.0, measuring login success, revocation cutoff, and verification latency under rollback.
PartitionRotate-30: software capabilities achieved 99.74% healthy-login success versus SecretBroker v1.0's 99.95%; TPM-clock contention caused verification timeouts.
Retain SecretBroker v1.0; reject software capabilities because TPM-clock contention reduced healthy-login success to 99.74%, below 99.9%.
Replace the software-capability prototype with SecretBroker v1.0 canaries testing HSM queue saturation, partitioned rotation, and rollback.
Deploy SecretBroker v1.0 to 1% regional canaries; inject 30-second partitions, broker rollback, rotation boundaries, and HSM queue load.
SecretBroker v1.1 adds canary rollout gates: block promotion below 99.9% healthy-login success or above 60-second revocation cutoff.
Replay PartitionRotate-30 against SecretBroker v1.1 and software capabilities; measure login success and revocation cutoff against promotion gates.
PartitionRotate-30 retest: batched TPM-clock reads raised software-capability login success from 99.74% to 99.93%, with 47-second revocation cutoff.
Can batched TPM-clock reads stay within two seconds of actual time under burst load and broker rollback?
250-ms TPM-clock batching with hardware-pinned sequence numbers keeps maximum clock error ≤2 seconds at 20,000 logins/s through rollback.
Move expiry checks to secure-NIC clocks using 45-second quorum-signed certificates and 90-second pre-staged rotation bundles.
Can secure-NIC clocks maintain ≤2-second expiry error through broker rollback and 30-second regional partitions?
Run ClockRollback-20k: compare secure-NIC and 250-ms batched TPM expiry error at 20,000 logins/s through 30-second partitions and rollback.
ClockRollback-20k: batched TPM maximum expiry error was 1.4 seconds at 20,000 logins/s through partitions and rollback.
Retain four-shard HSM gateways as primary (99.95% success); qualify batched-TPM fallback (99.93% success, 47-second cutoff, 1.4-second clock error).
Trigger batched-TPM fallback above 20-ms HSM p99 queue wait; pin revocation floors and canary failover through partitions and rollback.
Extend SecretBroker v1.1 canaries using HSM conformance fixtures; force 20-ms queue failover, partitioned rotation, and rollback; measure both SLOs.
SecretBroker v1.2 canary report records HSM-to-TPM failover, partitioned-rotation login success, rollback revocation cutoff, and promotion-gate outcomes.
Test secure-NIC expiry against SecretBroker v1.2 canary traces during partitions and rollback; compare login success, cutoff, clock error.
Secure-NIC canary replay achieved 99.96% healthy-login success, 48-second revocation cutoff, and 1.1-second maximum clock error.
Pilot secure-NIC expiry as an optional fast path; retain four-shard HSM gateways and batched-TPM fallback while validating rollout safety.
At 20,000 logins/s, secure-NIC expiry maintains ≤2-second clock error and ≥99.9% success during 30-second partitions and rollback.
Replay SecretBroker v1.2 canary traces at 20,000 logins/s with secure-NIC expiry; measure clock error and success through partitions and rollback.
At 20,000 logins/s, secure-NIC PTP resynchronization after partition caused 2.7-second clock error and 99.86% healthy-login success.
